$description: The Inspector's Content tab — what this element IS and what it says: its tag, id, class and text, its component settings, where it is used, its HTML attributes by section, and the attributes its schema does not know about. It is the densest surface in the application and it is drawn out of ONE row vocabulary: a section's body is a single list, and each entry names the shape it takes — a field, a key/value pair, a note, an action or a file. They differ in what they COMMIT rather than in what they look like, and what they commit is `panels/properties-panel.ts`'s decision, reached by the row's `key`. Nothing here knows what an attribute is, which cascade a value came from, or that a `$ref` is a binding: every field of every row is already a string, a flag or a list.

style.$description: What this block replaces is thirty-odd rules spread over `styles/inspector.css` and `styles/panels.css` — `.style-sidebar`, `.style-row`, `.style-row-label`, `.set-dot`, `.provenance-chip`, `.kv-row`, `.kv-add`, `.usage-row`, `.layout-origin*` and the teaching empty state — and they are TRANSCRIBED rather than shared, because a document emits no class and a class it does not emit cannot style it. The Style and Logic tabs still draw `.style-row`, so the stylesheet keeps those rules until they convert too. Two things changed on the way in. Every `--spectrum-font-size-*` is re-pointed at the kit's scale: this document is mounted in the Inspector's tab body, outside `<sp-theme>`, where each of those would have silently taken its hard-coded pixel fallback and stopped following the theme. And the provenance chip's four states are an ATTRIBUTE rather than four class names, because the state is a fact about the row's value and a document says such things with data.

& [part=\"empty\"].$description: The one empty-state pattern (`panels/empty-state.ts`), drawn here because a document cannot render a lit helper. Same three parts in the same order — the sentence saying what the region is for, the sentence saying where its content comes from, and the button that fills it.

& [part=\"section-body\"] > [part=\"row\.$description: §4.1's standard form row, stacked: the label sits above a control that takes the whole width. `min-width: 0` is what keeps it honest in a narrow dock — a field refuses to shrink below its own min-content without it. Scoped to the tab's OWN rows rather than to every `part="row"` beneath it, which a colour row made load-bearing: the kit is light DOM and one cascade, so a bare descendant selector also matches `jx-color-field`'s internal row — and at equal specificity with the kit's own `& > [part="row"]` the winner is whichever sheet was interned later, which is not a thing a stylesheet may depend on. `[part="chip"]` moved under `[part="chip-slot"]` for the same reason and a sharper one: its `background: transparent` and its border would otherwise have erased a swatch's colour and drawn a box round it. The `layout-class-slot` half of the pair is there because that slot is `display: contents`, so its row is a grandchild in the DOM even though it is a child in the box tree.

& [part=\"color-field\"] > [part=\"row\".$description: The field is `inline-flex` around a row sized to its own contents, which is wrong where the control IS the width of the dock. Two declarations, not a restatement of the kit's layout.

& [part=\"chip-slot\"] > [part=\"chip\"].$description: §6.2's provenance chip. `set` is the 6px accent dot it has always been — a circle is not a button, whatever element draws it — and the three states that carry a donor are bordered chips naming it. The fourth state, `default`, draws nothing at all: a ghost dot on every unset row says less than silence.

& [part=\"action\"].$description: The `.kv-add` affordance, which was a `<span>` with a click handler on it — not reachable by keyboard, and announced as nothing. It is a real button stripped of the chrome a button brings with it, so it still reads as a link at the foot of a section.

& [part=\"control-host\"].$description: `display: contents` for the reason every embedded host in this package uses it: the row lays its own children out, and a wrapper box would become the flex item in the control's place.

true.$description: Drawn only where it can run. A layout click focuses the pane it landed in — including a lens, which draws layout chrome because it draws the same document — and from a derived pane `pane.derive` can only refuse. A chip that does nothing when you press it is worse than no chip: the sentence above it already says where the element comes from.

children.$description: §6.2's collapsed-header tally. It is an indicator and not a control: the heading's own click already toggles the section, so a second meaning for the same click would be worse than the silence. It says how many values in the section are set, which is what a closed section otherwise cannot say.

true.$description: §6.3's Value Source chip: the rung this value is produced at, in plain language, opening a picker of every rung the POSITION permits. The rungs are derived from the schema at that position and the picker is the kit menu every other list in the shell opens, so neither is decided here.

link.$description: The Link target: a kind and a value, over one `href`. It is two controls because the attribute is two decisions — an internal route, an external URL, an anchor, an address or a number — and `utils/link-target.ts` is what joins them back into one string. The value half is a picker of the site's own routes when the kind is internal and a field otherwise, so the answer the author most often wants is the one they can pick.

color.$description: A prop whose schema says `format: "color"`. It was the second of the three lit leaves this tab drew into `[part="control-host"]`; `ui.md` §5.6 landed and it is `jx-color-field` here, beside every other control. The listener is on the WRAPPER and not on the field, and that is the field's own contract rather than a preference. `jx-color-field` stops its five inner controls' native events at its root and re-says the platform's two names FROM the host, so an ancestor hears exactly one `input` and one `change` per gesture with `e.target` being the field — while a listener on the field itself hears BOTH, including the raw `change` of a text box holding a half-typed word the field has just refused. Bound there, `not a colour` would have been committed as a colour.

true.$description: The palette's `change` is caught HERE, on the group, because it never gets out: the field routes it as its `palette` channel, stops it, and then declines it — a swatch that stands for `var(--color-accent)` is not a string the field can parse as a colour, which is exactly why the reference survives the click. A row that let the field answer instead would have committed the literal behind the token and quietly opted one declaration out of the palette for ever.

control.$description: The one thing still drawn in lit. The media picker, the colour selector and the expression editor are each their own surface with readers outside this tab, so the document draws an empty host and `panels/properties-panel.ts` renders into it — the seam `ui/schema-form.ts` established for a registered control. The host is announced through `onNodeCreated` as it is created, never found by selector.

kv.$description: An editable key/value pair — a custom attribute, which is a name and a value and a way to be rid of it. Both cells commit through the same debounce as every other text control, so renaming a key and retyping its value in one gesture is one write.
